# FAB

The one primary action of a screen, floating over its content at the bottom inline-end corner.

**Not implemented yet.** This page is the *approved intent* — the props API signed off at gate 1 of the build order, before any React exists. Do not import it; there is nothing to import.

| | |
|---|---|
| Registry name | `fab` |
| Family | buttons |
| Tier | free |
| Status (css / react / figma) | future / future / future |
| Depends on | `button`, `state-layer`, `spinner`, `icon` |

## Behavior

A `<button type="button">` fixed to a corner of the viewport, with Button's activation, loading and disabled behaviour. No primitive of its own: it composes `getButtonProps`, because activation is identical and a second implementation of it is a second place for the aria-disabled guard to go wrong.

- **It is a component, not a Button with a className** — This system's test for a new component is a difference in semantics, and a FAB has none: it is announced as a button and activated as one. What it adds is a placement that every consumer would otherwise hand-write — fixed to a corner, offset by the safe-area inset, lifted clear of a BottomNav — and that is exactly the kind of value that ends up as `bottom: 72px` in a stylesheet and wrong on the next phone. It composes Button's primitive rather than restating it, so the only new thing is the geometry.
- **One per screen, and always the primary fill — so there is no `variant`** — A FAB says 'this is what this screen is for'. Two of them say nothing, and a secondary-styled one is a primary action that has been told to look unimportant while still floating over everything. The fill is Button's primary pair because it is the primary action; a destructive action never floats, because the one control that is always under the thumb is the last one that should delete something.
- **`label` is required and shown by default** — A floating glyph is the least explained control on a screen: it is detached from any content that could give it context. So the label is visible unless `labelHidden` is set, the same default and the same prop name as Switch. When it is hidden it becomes the `aria-label`, and it is still required, because an icon-only button with no name is announced as 'button' — this is Button's `iconOnly` obligation, enforced by the type instead of the contract.
- **It does not shrink or hide on scroll** — Collapsing a labelled FAB to its icon on scroll, or sliding it off-screen, is common and has the problem BottomNav's contract names: it moves a target out from under a thumb that was about to use it. It also changes the accessible name's visibility mid-gesture. The vertical space it saves is one control's worth in one corner.
- **Reading order follows the DOM, so where it is rendered matters more than where it floats** — Fixed positioning moves the paint and not the tab order. Rendered after a long list, the FAB is reached by keyboard only after every row in it; rendered at the start of `<main>`, it is reached first, which matches its importance. The contract cannot choose this for the caller, so it says it: render it before the content it acts on.
- **It covers content, and the page reserves space for that** — A fixed control sits over whatever scrolls beneath it, so the last row of a list ends behind it. BottomNav avoids this by being sticky; a FAB cannot, because it floats in a corner rather than spanning an edge. The page's scrolling content needs `padding-block-end` of at least the FAB's block size plus its offset — the recipe states both in tokens, so the reservation is a sum of the same tokens rather than a measured number.
- **A speed dial is a Menu, not a mode of this** — A FAB that fans out into three smaller actions is a trigger and a transient list of actions, which is precisely Menu — focus moves into it, Escape returns to the trigger, the arrow keys move between items. `<Menu trigger={<Fab … />}>` gets all of that from a component that already owns it; a `speedDial` prop here would be a second, unreviewed menu.
- **`loading` and `disabled` behave exactly as they do on Button** — Both are aria-disabled: the FAB stays focusable and discoverable and activation is blocked in the primitive. `loading` shows a Spinner in place of the icon and keeps the label, so the FAB does not change size while an action is pending. They are mutually exclusive for Button's reason — a control cannot be both busy and unavailable.
- **Token gap: size.target.min — needs the design-tokens skill** — A FAB is a thumb target and should be at least 48px; the size scale stops at `size.control.lg`, 36px. The recipe composes `size.control.lg` plus `space.1-5` on each side as a stand-in, which lands on 48px by arithmetic rather than by rule. The same gap is flagged in BottomNav, ListItem and Chip; one `size.target.min` token would close all four.
- **Token gap: theme.elevation.floating — needs the design-tokens skill** — The elevation roles are named by situation and none is this one. `raised` is a resting card that is part of the page; `overlay` is a transient surface anchored to a trigger; `modal` takes over the screen. A FAB is persistent, like `raised`, and floats over moving content, which `raised`'s shadow is too soft to read against. The recipe uses `overlay` as the closest that is visible over scrolling content, which is a misuse by its own documentation — a `theme.elevation.floating` role with its own dark-scheme `-strong` twin would say what this actually is.
- **Web and native** — On the web it renders `<button type="button">`, position fixed, with `aria-label={label}` only when `labelHidden` is set — otherwise the visible text is the name, and the icon is `aria-hidden`. While `loading` it carries `aria-disabled="true"` and `aria-busy="true"`. On React Native it renders a `Pressable` with `accessibilityRole="button"`, `accessibilityLabel={label}`, and `accessibilityState={{ disabled, busy: loading }}`, absolutely positioned inside the screen and offset by `useSafeAreaInsets()`. Web-only: `className`, and the BottomNav clearance, which is a CSS `:has()` rule — a native screen knows its tab bar's height from the navigator and offsets by that instead. No prop is native-only. There is no gesture.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string` | — | What the action does, as a verb phrase — shown beside the icon, or used as the accessible name when hidden. |
| `icon` | `LucideIcon` | — | The glyph, which is always shown. |
| `labelHidden?` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows the icon alone, as a circle, with `label` as the accessible name. |
| `placement?` | `"end" \| "center"` | `"end"` | Which bottom corner it floats at — inline-end, or centred. |
| `loading?` | `boolean` | — | Shows a Spinner in place of the icon and blocks activation, while staying focusable. |
| `disabled?` | `boolean` | — | Blocks activation while keeping it focusable and announced. |
| `className?` | `string` | — | Extra classes, for placement adjustments — not for restyling it. |

### `label`

```ts
label: string
```

What the action does, as a verb phrase — shown beside the icon, or used as the accessible name when hidden.

**Use when**

- A short imperative: 'Compose', 'New invoice', 'Add photo'.

**Don't use for**

- A noun alone ('Invoice'), which says what the screen is about rather than what the button does.

**Accessibility** The accessible name in both states. Visible text when shown; `aria-label` when `labelHidden` is set.

### `icon`

```ts
icon: LucideIcon
```

The glyph, which is always shown.

**Use when**

- A glyph that means the action on its own — a plus for create, a pencil for compose.

**Don't use for**

- A brand mark or an illustration. Above `size.icon.lg` a graphic is no longer an icon, and the FAB's size is fixed.

**Accessibility** Decorative: `aria-hidden`, because `label` is the name.

### `labelHidden`

```ts
labelHidden?: boolean = false
```

Shows the icon alone, as a circle, with `label` as the accessible name.

**Use when**

- An action so conventional on its screen that the glyph explains it — the plus on a list of notes.

**Don't use for**

- Saving space on a screen where the action is not obvious. The label is what explains a floating control, and a circle with a glyph in it saves one word's width.

**Accessibility** The name does not change; only whether it is visible.

### `placement`

```ts
placement?: "end" | "center" = "end"
```

Which bottom corner it floats at — inline-end, or centred.

**Use when**

- `center` when the screen's content is symmetrical and the action belongs to all of it, such as a camera's shutter.

**Don't use for**

- `center` above a BottomNav. It lands over the middle destination's label and reads as a sixth item.

**Accessibility** Visual only; reading order follows the DOM, not the corner.

### `loading`

```ts
loading?: boolean
```

Shows a Spinner in place of the icon and blocks activation, while staying focusable.

**Use when**

- The action's request is in flight and a second press would send it twice.

**Don't use for**

- As a page-loading indicator. The FAB is busy only with its own action.

**Conflicts with** `disabled`

**Accessibility** `aria-disabled="true"` and `aria-busy="true"`, as on Button. The label stays, so the name does not change while it is pending.

### `disabled`

```ts
disabled?: boolean
```

Blocks activation while keeping it focusable and announced.

**Use when**

- The action exists on this screen but cannot run yet, and the reader should be able to find out it exists.

**Don't use for**

- Permanently. A FAB that can never be pressed on a screen should not be rendered there — a disabled control floating over everything is the most prominent thing on the screen, and it does nothing.

**Conflicts with** `loading`

**Accessibility** `aria-disabled`, not the `disabled` attribute, so it stays in the tab order and screen readers announce it as unavailable rather than skipping it.

### `className`

```ts
className?: string
```

Extra classes, for placement adjustments — not for restyling it.

**Use when**

- Hiding it at widths where the action lives in a toolbar instead.

**Don't use for**

- A hand-written `bottom` offset. The placement is computed from the safe area and the BottomNav; a fixed number is wrong on the next device.

## Use cases

### Creating the thing a list is a list of

A screen that is mostly one collection, where adding to it is the reason the screen exists.

```tsx
<Fab label="New note" icon={Plus} onClick={createNote} />
```

Rendered at the start of `<main>`, before the list, so a keyboard reaches it first. The list reserves `padding-block-end` so its last row is not left under the FAB.

### A conventional glyph with the label hidden

The action is the one every reader of this screen expects, and the glyph is its well-known mark.

```tsx
<Fab label="Compose" icon={Pencil} labelHidden onClick={compose} />
```

`label` is still required: it becomes the `aria-label`. Hiding it is the exception, not the default, because nothing near a floating control explains it.

### Several creation actions behind one FAB

A screen where the primary action is 'add', and there are two or three kinds of thing to add.

```tsx
<Menu label="Add" trigger={<Fab label="Add" icon={Plus} />}>
  <MenuItem onSelect={addPhoto}>Photo</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem onSelect={addNote}>Note</MenuItem>
</Menu>
```

This is the speed dial, and it is Menu's job: focus moves into the list, Escape returns to the FAB, arrow keys move between items.

### Reaching for the wrong component: two floating actions

A screen with a primary action and a secondary one, both wanting to float.

```tsx
<Fab label="Save" icon={Check} />
<Fab label="Discard" icon={X} />
```

Don't. Two FABs is no primary action. Discard is not something to keep under the thumb at all — it belongs in a footer or a Menu, as a Button or a destructive MenuItem.

## Token recipe

### base

A primary button in shape and colour, held to a corner of the viewport. The fill and its label token are Button's primary pair unchanged, because this is the screen's primary action and nothing about floating changes that.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| background | `theme.accent-role.bg` |
| color | `theme.fg.on-accent — the one label token that belongs on theme.accent-role.bg` |
| block-size | `size.control.lg plus space.1-5 above and below (48px) — a stand-in for the touch-target minimum this system has no token for; see the token-gap decision` |
| inline-size, label hidden | `equal to the block-size, so the hidden-label FAB is a circle` |
| padding-inline, label visible | `space.control.padding-inline.lg` |
| border-radius | `radius.pill — one radius that makes the hidden-label FAB a circle and the labelled one a pill, so the two are visibly the same control` |
| box-shadow | `theme.elevation.overlay — a stand-in; see the token-gap decision` |
| icon size | `size.icon.lg` |
| gap between icon and label | `space.gap.sm` |
| font-size | `type.control.size.md` |
| font-weight | `type.control.weight` |
| line-height | `type.control.line-height.md` |
| hover / press | `compose the .rata-state-layer class — do not swap the background` |
| focus ring | `theme.focus-ring at focus.ring-width, offset focus.ring-offset, on :focus-visible — never offset 0, because this is a filled accent control` |
| disabled | `state.disabled-opacity, on aria-disabled` |
| transition-duration | `motion.interactive.duration` |
| transition-timing-function | `motion.interactive.easing` |

### placement

Where it floats. Measured from the viewport's safe area rather than its edge, and lifted clear of a BottomNav when one is on the page.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| position | `fixed` |
| inset-inline-end | `max(space.padding.md, env(safe-area-inset-right) plus space.padding.md)` |
| inset-block-end | `max(space.padding.md, env(safe-area-inset-bottom) plus space.padding.md)` |
| placement center | `inset-inline-start 50% with a translate of half its own inline size, in place of inset-inline-end` |
| clearance above a BottomNav | `when `:root:has(.rata-bottom-nav)`, inset-block-end adds the bar's own block size — computed from the same tokens BottomNav's recipe uses, so nothing is measured at runtime` |
| z-index | `above page content and below the top layer — a Dialog, Sheet or Menu opened from it must cover it, and they do, because the top layer is above every z-index` |
